key_insight: Abductive learning can reinforce incorrect concept meanings, and optimization geometry can determine which explanation training selects even under identical supervision, objectives, and initialization.
engineering_relevance: Constraint satisfaction alone does not guarantee correct learned concepts, so ABL systems should monitor concept accuracy and sensitivity to optimizer choice.
method: Analyze training dynamics in a fixed-feature binary ABL model.
Link competing explanations’ local stability to differences in their concept labels.
Prove explanation-selection and stability results, then test predictions on visual ABL tasks.
evidence_signal: Visual ABL experiments show attraction to incorrect concepts under identifiable supervision, different explanation selection by SGD and Adam, and declining unseen-concept accuracy as training concept errors grow.
watch_item: The formal guarantees rely on a fixed-feature binary model and specific assumptions; they should not be generalized automatically to end-to-end ABL systems.
